rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for meaning ‘for a long time’.

example.english: I've been waiting for you for a long time.
example.jyutping: ngo5 dang2 zo2 nei5 hou2 noi6 laa3

rows.note: Use this when the state or action has continued throughout the period up to now or another reference point.

example.english: They have long lived in this neighborhood.
example.jyutping: keoi5 jat1 zik6 dou1 zyu6 hai2 ni1 keoi1

rows.note: Use this mainly in formal or written wording for an extended period.

example.english: This policy has long remained effective.
example.jyutping: goi1 zing3 caak3 coeng4 kei4 jau5 haau6

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for physical length and for things such as speeches, films, or books that have excessive duration.

example.jyutping: ni1 tiu4 kwan4 taai3 coeng4 laa3

rows.note: Use this for an event or activity that continues for a long time, especially when emphasizing the elapsed time.

example.english: The movie was really long; it didn't let out until three hours later.
example.traditional: 呢套戲真係耐，成三個鐘先散場。
example.jyutping: ni1 tou3 hei3 zan1 hai6 noi6 sing4 saam1 go3 zung1 sin1 saan3 coeng4

rows.note: Use this when something is distant in time, such as the distant past or distant future.

example.english: Those events happened a long time ago, and I can no longer remember them.
example.traditional: 嗰段遙遠嘅往事，我已經唔記得喇。
example.jyutping: go2 dyun6 jiu4 jyun5 ge3 wong5 si6 ngo5 ji5 ging1 m4 gei3 dak1 laa3
